task.title: kelpie: park returns a task to the refine queue

ask: When you park a task, it goes back to be agreed again, instead of waiting for you to mark it Refined by hand.

demo.scope: The kelpie CLI's park and what status and the next tick do after it. A fixture for demo-viz: past work (563236a), re-run as if just finished. The sign-off half of that commit (a refine sign-off keeps unshipped work) isn't walked through; its tests cover it.

before.text: Parks a task, then has to remember to mark it Refined by hand; it sits in its own Parked row.
before.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 200 60" role="img" aria-label="A terminal"><rect x="4" y="4" width="192" height="52" rx="6" fill="#0d1117" stroke="#8b93a7"/></svg>

after.text: Parking sends the task straight back to the refine queue, to be agreed again.

assumptions.text: The task's folder and branch stay, so the next run picks up the work so far.

examples.text: Parking a task mid-build, with your words, puts them on the task and sends it back to the refine queue, to be agreed again.
The build slot is free straight away, and status no longer has a Parked row.
On the next tick Kelpie starts a refine run for it, in the same folder.
A parked task goes back to the build queue with its old sign-off.

plan.step: park resets the run's history and unrefines the task; drop the Parked row.
